rule: GOAL: Reproduce the target sequence shown at the top by placing the correct colors into the empty slots. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click a slot to place it. RULE: Match the specific order of colors displayed in the outlined row at the top of the screen. TRAP: Assuming the palette order matches the target order; always verify the top sequence before placing colors.

GOAL: Align the yellow handle with the gap in the black wall to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: The top blue button shifts the upper boundary left and the lower boundary right. The bottom blue button shifts the upper boundary right and the lower boundary left. RULE: Clicking a blue button moves the boundaries in opposite directions, dragging the attached yellow handle along with the lower boundary. TRAP: Assuming the yellow handle moves independently. It is attached to the lower boundary, so you must move the boundary to position the handle.

GOAL: Fill the red frame by inserting the green block into its open slot to complete the sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette colors to place them into empty slots; press Space to submit the solution. RULE: The green block acts as a nested unit, replacing the red frame's third slot rather than appending to the end. TRAP: Assuming the flat order was simply all red slots followed by all green slots, which ignores the port's interior position.

GOAL: Guide the hero from the start room to the exit room within a shrinking time budget. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the hero one room at a time; doors open automatically when approached. RULE: Movement is strictly one room per press, not sliding until a wall, so plan each step carefully. TRAP: Assuming you slide through open doors wastes time; you must press an arrow for every room transition.

GOAL: Fill all slots to match the top sequence order. CONTROLS: Click colors from the bottom palette, then click empty slots. Press space to submit. RULE: Read left to right; when hitting a colored port, fill that matching box’s slots before continuing the main row. TRAP: Ignoring port colors and filling boxes sequentially by position rather than by their specific color tag.

GOAL: Move the blue bar to block the laser, then trigger the magenta fill to plug the bottom notch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the bar horizontally; Space activates the laser and fill sequence. RULE: The magenta column stops exactly where the laser beam is intercepted by the bar. TRAP: Thinking the bar must sit inside the notch itself; it must instead catch the laser from above to direct the flow.

GOAL: Move the purple square to the top ball using limited clicks. CONTROLS: Click a dot on the path to swap positions with the square, moving it forward. RULE: You can only move to an adjacent dot; clicking further away does nothing. TRAP: Believing you could jump multiple steps or click the square itself to move.

GOAL: Flatten nested boxes by inserting a sub-list port into the parent list. CONTROLS: Click palette to select, click slot to place, space to confirm. RULE: Attach the green box port into the red list's empty slot to expand the sequence. TRAP: Assuming slots are fixed; you must first insert the port to create room for nested items.

GOAL: Turn every lever black to solve the puzzle. CONTROLS: Clicking a lever toggles its color between white and black. RULE: The level is solved only when all ten horizontal and vertical levers are set to black. TRAP: Believing the bouncing ball animation indicated movement or progress, when it was merely a decorative idle effect.

GOAL: Clear the level in four clicks by shrinking the middle panel until it vanished. CONTROLS: Clicking below the walls shrank the adjacent white panels, moving their edges leftward. RULE: The middle panel shrank by a fixed width each time until it disappeared completely. TRAP: Believing the panel would vanish in one click cost time, as it required multiple distinct reductions to clear.

GOAL: Fit a three-slot blue box into a five-slot red line using two ports, leaving exactly three red slots empty to match the total item count. CONTROLS: Click items to drag them from the side palette into the numbered slots or onto the ports to attach them. RULE: The sequence of colors visible through the ports must be identical, forcing the blue box's contents to mirror the hidden red positions. TRAP: Assuming ports could go anywhere; only specific adjacent slots allowed the total visible items to equal the available palette count.

GOAL: Match three color-coded boxes to the top row's sequence by assigning ports to red slots. CONTROLS: Drag ports to red slots; drag tiles to box slots; press space to submit. RULE: Each box's contents must exactly match its corresponding chunk of the top row. TRAP: Assuming port order is fixed; you must manually assign ports to align with the row's groups.

GOAL: Guide the head to absorb scattered gems and deposit them into matching slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block four spaces and flip the head to the facing edge; Space absorbs or deposits adjacent items. RULE: The head must face the target box to absorb it, but carrying a payload prevents the head from flipping during movement. TRAP: Assuming movement rotates the shape while carrying a gem wastes time; the block only translates until you deposit the payload.

GOAL: Match five blue glyphs to their pink counterparts using a visual legend. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selector; confirm locks a match. RULE: Each blue shape corresponds to the pink shape sharing its unique closed-hole pattern. TRAP: Assuming the legend pairs were subset-related rather than identity mappings wasted early moves.

GOAL: Shift liquid to align three handles at specific heights. CONTROLS: Left and right buttons moved liquid between adjacent tanks. RULE: Flow was blocked if a tank reached its maximum capacity. TRAP: Assuming all tanks could hold excess liquid led to dead ends when middle tanks overflowed.

GOAL: Paint the panel's white cells green to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; clicks toggle cell colors; specific inputs transmit the pattern. RULE: The level completes only when the panel's green cells exactly match the displayed target. TRAP: Believing the moving tip or knob position was the objective, rather than the static panel match.

GOAL: Align three horizontal bars to form a continuous channel that guides falling fluid into the target notch below. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the selected bar horizontally or vertically; mouse clicks switch control to a different bar; spacebar releases the fluid. RULE: Only the currently highlighted bar responds to movement commands, requiring you to click each bar individually to position it correctly. TRAP: Assuming all bars move simultaneously or that the last clicked bar remains active causes misalignment and wasted turns.

GOAL: Flatten nested boxes to match the top row pattern. CONTROLS: Drag ports to link boxes; drag items to fill slots; press space to check. RULE: A port placed in a parent slot expands the child box’s contents into that position. TRAP: Thinking ports only connect outer boxes; they must nest inside each other to reveal the center.

GOAL: The puzzle required shrinking a wide block to fit through a narrow gate. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block; clicking panel cells changed its size. RULE: Matching the panel pattern to the target color toggled the block’s state. TRAP: Assuming the block could slide freely until touching the gate; it stopped short, requiring a size change first.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the red enemy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one space; the red enemy reacts to movement. RULE: The enemy lunges toward you if you move in its row, covering the same distance you moved. TRAP: Assuming the enemy is a static wall or a collectible item, rather than a dynamic threat that tracks your movement distance.

GOAL: Match each slot’s symbol to the legend by cycling through dial states. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; DOWN cycles the selected slot’s symbol forward. RULE: Only symbol identity matters; rotation is a visual distractor, not a constraint. TRAP: Assuming rotation changes meaning wastes time; focus solely on matching the correct glyph shape.

GOAL: Merge two squares into one yellow square positioned over the central ball. CONTROLS: Click near a square to move it one step toward the cursor location. RULE: A merge occurs automatically when the moving square comes within eight units of the stationary square. TRAP: Assuming you must click exactly on the target center; clicking slightly off is safer and still triggers the merge.

ESTABLISHED: The arm drags blocks left to the home column. FAILED: Moving the head without retracting pushes parked blocks right. GOAL IS NOT: Pulling blocks into the head itself. CONTROLS: Up/Down moves the head; Left/Right extends/retracts the arm to grab or release blocks.

GOAL: Decode the hidden message to set the blue dial to the matching color sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selector; pressing down rotates the current dial forward through its cycle. RULE: Each dial has a fixed seven-state loop including one decoy; calculate the shortest path to the target color. TRAP: Assuming all seven states are valid colors wastes time; ignore the decoy state when planning your moves.

GOAL: Route the tip through a newly opened arm to the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; special actions clear obstacles or unlock paths. RULE: Clearing the central block removes the path to the knob, forcing travel along the extended arm. TRAP: Assuming black gaps are passable wastes time; they act as solid walls preventing direct descent.

GOAL: Merge two separated particles into one shape, then deliver it and a second particle to their matching targets. CONTROLS: Clicking near a piece moves it closer to the click point; clicking near two pieces merges them if within range. RULE: A single click affects only the nearest piece, so position clicks carefully to control which object moves. TRAP: Assuming you can move both pieces simultaneously or that merge range is larger than the safe distance tested.

GOAL: Transform bottom blue glyphs through a two-step chain to match target yellow shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows cycled the selection dial to choose the correct transformation output. RULE: Apply the S-to-P mapping first, then the P-to-Y mapping to find the final symbol. TRAP: Assuming the target symbol was visible in the bottom row; you must check the full legend for missing labels.

GOAL: Align cross arms with colored dots to cover them. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cross; space confirms placement. RULE: The cross must cover all dots of one color to clear it. TRAP: Over-movement causes misalignment, wasting actions and requiring repositioning.

GOAL: Grow the green bar until its red tip lands precisely on the target plus sign. CONTROLS: Click the side panel to extend the bar by three units per action. RULE: The bar length must allow the red marker to align exactly with the plus's center. TRAP: Believing the bar tip itself needed to touch the plus, ignoring the marker's offset.

GOAL: Reach the exit by destroying red enemies with direct movement. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Moving onto a red enemy destroys it and occupies its space. TRAP: Do not assume a no-op report means failure; verify board state, as moves often succeed despite harness errors.

GOAL: Move colored shapes to cover matching dots, using seven actions. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected shape; Space switched selection. RULE: Shapes only fit if their center aligns with a dot cluster. TRAP: Thinking occlusion breaks logic; hidden pixels still count for alignment.

GOAL: Rotate the glyph to match the target pattern, then push the block into the black box. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the block; passing over the plus sign rotates the glyph shape. RULE: The glyph must match the target pattern exactly at the moment the block enters the box. TRAP: Assuming matching the pattern anywhere wins; you must physically deliver the correct shape into the goal zone.

GOAL: Align the yellow square with the fixed yellow bracket. CONTROLS: Left arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; right arrow rotates clockwise. RULE: Each click moves every item one step, shifting the target into position. TRAP: Assuming symmetry matters; only the single highlighted spot dictates the win.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single piece by jumping over others. CONTROLS: Click a piece to highlight valid landing spots, then click a highlighted spot to jump. RULE: A jump requires an adjacent opponent piece and an empty space directly beyond it. TRAP: Assuming the goal was to reach a specific location rather than simply clearing all but one piece.

GOAL: Place four shapes over dots using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected shape; Space cycles selection. RULE: Shapes rotate in fixed order; move each to cover its dot. TRAP: Assuming shapes move independently; cycling order dictates sequence, wasting moves if misordered.

GOAL: Guide the mirrored twin to the exit using a single action sequence. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved both squares simultaneously. RULE: Horizontal commands were reversed for the second square, while vertical commands remained identical. TRAP: Assuming both squares obeyed the same left-right directions caused immediate collisions and wasted moves.

GOAL: Match the bottom-right panel's cell colors to the small pattern shown in its center. CONTROLS: Clicking a grid cell toggled its color between blue and red. RULE: White dots in the center pattern meant red cells; gray dots meant blue. TRAP: Assuming clicks affected neighboring cells like Lights Out; only the clicked cell changed.

GOAL: Match the grid to the dial patterns by turning cells orange. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between blue and orange. RULE: The dial’s center color defines the target; white maps to that color, green to blue. TRAP: Assuming each dial acts independently; they actually overlap, so one dial’s bottom row must match the other’s top row.

GOAL: Guide two blocks into their matching rings. CONTROLS: Arrows push blocks; clicks toggle doors. RULE: Blocks stop when hitting walls or ring frames, not passing through. TRAP: Assuming ring cells are empty space; they block movement until aligned.

GOAL: Match the grid to the overlapping dial patterns. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle colors. RULE: White marks show the dial's center color; grey marks show the other color. TRAP: Assuming overlapping dials conflict, when they actually define the same color for shared cells.

GOAL: Align both yellow markers onto the two cursor positions simultaneously. CONTROLS: Top arrows rotate the large outer ring. Middle and bottom arrows shift their respective horizontal rows left or right. RULE: Moving a row also rotates the specific ring segments embedded in it, coupling the horizontal and circular movements. TRAP: Assuming row shifts only affect straight lines ignores how they drag ring cells, causing misalignment of the shared corner pieces.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking dots swaps ball positions; the square relocates to the midpoint between them. FAILED: Clicking the ring center or distant empty cells produces no change. GOAL IS NOT: Merging the balls or reaching the ring with the square. CONTROLS: Clicking a dot moves a ball there; clicking elsewhere is invalid.

GOAL: Guide the two blocks until they stand side-by-side. CONTROLS: Arrows move the left block normally and the right block in the opposite direction. RULE: Once horizontally adjacent, a single rightward push swaps their positions to merge. TRAP: Assuming vertical alignment wins; you must force a horizontal collision to succeed.

GOAL: Move each token to its matching colored bracket. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows shift all tokens along their respective tracks. RULE: Every token must land on the bracket of its own color simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming arrow directions match visual orientation; test clicks to learn actual movement signs.

GOAL: Guide two crosshairs to cover matching colored dots while ensuring each crosshair adopts the correct color from specific docking squares. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active crosshair; spacebar switches control between the crosshair and the plus symbol. RULE: A crosshair permanently changes color when it rests on a matching colored square, a state that persists even after it moves away. TRAP: Believing crosshairs must start at the correct color; failing to move them to the source squares first prevents the win condition.

GOAL: Place the square inside the matching purple ring to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click near the white ball to move it; click near the gray ball to swap their positions. RULE: Swapping only works if you click a spot within two rows of the gray ball. TRAP: Moving the white ball directly to the ring fails; you must swap first to align the square.

ESTABLISHED: The snake has shifted, clearing the left corridor and bottom path to the goal. FAILED: Waiting for the snake to move independently; it only reacts to player input. GOAL IS NOT: To destroy the snake or reach its head; the exit is open. CONTROLS: Moving left, down, or right shifts the player and advances the snake one segment.

GOAL: Move the yellow token to the center bracket and the purple token to the right bracket. CONTROLS: Click arrows to slide tokens in that direction; tokens share rows or columns. RULE: Brackets mark exact target cells, not just general zones; check pixel alignment carefully. TRAP: Assuming the right bracket covered the middle-right cell instead of the far-right cell caused wasted moves.

GOAL: Color the grid cells to satisfy the overlapping color constraints of the scattered dials. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color through blue, red, and orange. RULE: A cell must match the center color of any dial where it sits in the marked white zone. TRAP: Assuming cells covered by multiple dials need a neutral third color; they actually require the shared center color.

GOAL: Guide two yellow tokens to the highlighted brackets at opposite corners of the top row. CONTROLS: Top arrows rotate only the five top cells; middle arrows rotate the large twenty-one-cell outer loop. RULE: The top row acts as a separate five-cell ring that overlaps the larger loop, allowing independent positioning. TRAP: Assuming middle controls rotate the whole board wastes moves; they strictly follow the long perimeter, ignoring the inner top row shift.

GOAL: Align the black shape’s dots with the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the black shape; pressing LEFT shifts the charcoal right, and DOWN shifts both down. RULE: Horizontal controls are mirrored: press LEFT to move the charcoal right. TRAP: Believing RIGHT moves the charcoal right wasted time, as it actually pulls it left.

GOAL: Align the plug's tips with the distant green terminals to connect the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug horizontally or vertically across the grid. RULE: The plug connects when its tip coordinates exactly match the terminal positions. TRAP: Assuming you can batch all moves at once risks wasting inputs if the level ends early.

GOAL: Align the falling shape with the static target zone to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space switches control focus between pieces. RULE: Only the piece holding the cursor responds to directional input. TRAP: Assuming all pieces move simultaneously when pressing arrows, rather than just the focused one.

GOAL: Navigate the green plug to A's yellow knob to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; clicking sockets toggles red arms horizontal/vertical and blue zones solid/checker. RULE: Solid blue blocks passage; checker blue allows it; red arms act as walls when horizontal, floors when vertical. TRAP: Believing red arms are always passable; they block movement when horizontal but become traversable only when vertical.

GOAL: Merge two purple pieces into a yellow one and deliver it to the target. CONTROLS: Click empty spaces to move pieces; click between overlapping pieces to merge them. RULE: Merging preserves material, demoting purple to yellow, so nothing is lost to the invader. TRAP: Thinking the invader destroys material permanently; it only moves pieces, so merging is safe.

GOAL: Place two black shapes so their mirrored reflections exactly cover the yellow target zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches between the two shapes. RULE: Each shape casts a reflection across the central horizontal bar; both the shape and its reflection must land on yellow targets simultaneously. TRAP: Forgetting that moving one shape also moves its reflection, causing misalignment if you ignore the mirrored position.

GOAL: Slide the green socket to the target while keeping the blue plug aligned with its new tips. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; clicks switch focus to the connected plug. RULE: The plug does not automatically follow the socket; you must manually reposition both to maintain alignment. TRAP: Assuming the plug moves with the socket wastes time trying to click or move the wrong piece.

GOAL: Align all shapes and reflections to cover the yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected object; Space cycles selection between objects. RULE: Reflections mirror across the central bar, so positioning relative to the axis is critical. TRAP: Assuming objects cannot pass through the bar or each other wastes time; overlaps are allowed.

GOAL: Set the grid so orthogonal neighbors match the button's base color, while diagonal neighbors take the alternate color. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle their color state until they match the required pattern. RULE: The button's base color defines the "primary" hue; its pattern marks which neighbors share that primary hue versus the secondary hue. TRAP: Assuming the button's base color was fixed or irrelevant; in reality, it defines the absolute target colors for all surrounding cells.

ESTABLISHED: The target is not full-bottom coverage; the cavity is eight rows deep, but the die only sinks five. FAILED: Four presses with a white top left uncovered areas near the center that the die physically cannot reach. GOAL IS NOT: Turning the entire bottom half purple, as the die's fixed depth makes this geometrically impossible. CONTROLS: Pressing the mold sinks it five rows; tilting rotates the diamond shape but does not extend the die's vertical reach.

ESTABLISHED: The black matrix is solid. Removing the upper plug filled exactly 35 cells, confirming adjacent matrix blocks are impermeable. FAILED: Clicking distant plugs to clear paths for lateral movement has not worked. GOAL IS NOT: Rising vertically through the left plug stack, as downward paths are blocked by solid matrix. CONTROLS: Clicking removes plugs; water fills freed space only if adjacent to existing water.

GOAL: Reach the pink shape at the far end of the upper chamber. CONTROLS: Click removed the barrier block. Arrow keys moved the player horizontally. RULE: Removing the barrier allowed the player to float up through the channel to the surface. TRAP: Thinking you could walk directly to the goal or that the pink shape was an enemy to avoid.

GOAL: Recolor the diamond red by driving it into the right-side well. CONTROLS: Arrows move the diamond; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: Overlapping two or more cells of a well triggers a color change. TRAP: Moving straight up from the blue well clipped the north well, accidentally turning the diamond blue.

GOAL: Guide two yellow cars into separate dead-end parking spots using only arrow keys. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected car; clicking a gray square selects or deselects a car. RULE: Cars slide until hitting a wall or another car, so plan paths that stop exactly in the target slots. TRAP: Assuming you can turn freely mid-slide; a single directional input moves the car all the way to the next obstacle, not one cell.

GOAL: Arrange horizontal bars so their gaps align perfectly with fixed source notches to let light pass through. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it, use arrow keys to move it, and press space to test the configuration. RULE: Bars must not overlap; moving one bar often requires shifting others first to clear a path for alignment. TRAP: Assuming all bars can move freely; ignoring collision rules wastes moves trying to force bars through each other.

GOAL: Place the square marker inside the orange ring. CONTROLS: Click a ball to move it; click a dot to hop to another ball. RULE: The square’s center aligns with the average position of all balls. TRAP: Assuming you could place the square directly; you had to hop between balls to shift the average.

GOAL: Position two mirror axes to reflect the shape, filling all yellow gaps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected object; Space cycles selection between shape and axes. RULE: Axes reflect the shape across their line; two perpendicular axes generate four symmetric copies. TRAP: Assuming one axis suffices wastes time; you must adjust both the horizontal and vertical bars to complete the symmetry.

GOAL: Move two mirrored agents until they occupy the same cell. CONTROLS: Arrows move both agents simultaneously; one follows input, the other mirrors it. RULE: Win instantly when both agents target the exact same coordinate. TRAP: Assuming blocked moves stop both agents; obstacles halt only the impacted agent, breaking synchronization.

GOAL: Reach the yellow exit by climbing the red arm mechanism. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; clicking the red socket rotates the arms. RULE: The player must stand on the dark red center while clicking to rotate the arms into a vertical path. TRAP: Assuming arms stay horizontal; failing to rotate them upward first blocks all progress to the exit.

GOAL: Form the letter P using two balls and specific grid constraints. CONTROLS: Click a ball to select it, then click a target cell to move it. RULE: The letter’s center must align with the designated anchor point on the grid. TRAP: Assuming balls could pass through others; they cannot, forcing complex rerouting around the N shape.

GOAL: Move three yellow tokens to matching target slots before locking the frame. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotated tokens around their cluster; number keys shifted tokens inward or outward. RULE: Each token had its own center point, so moving one never disturbed the others. TRAP: Thinking the rotation direction was uniform; one cluster actually rotated opposite to the others, requiring reverse inputs.

GOAL: Align two mirror-image shapes and position bars to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Click shapes to select them; use arrow keys to move selected pieces. RULE: Shapes must match their reflected counterparts exactly; bars align to grid axes. TRAP: Re-clicking an already selected piece counts as a wasted action, stalling progress.

GOAL: Align tokens on the vertical column using a limited action budget. CONTROLS: Up and Down arrows cyclically shifted the three tokens in the vertical strip. RULE: Each arrow press rotated the column tokens one step, consuming the shrinking green bar. TRAP: Believing arrows affected the horizontal row wasted turns; they only rotated the vertical trio.

GOAL: Move all three balls to form a valid square on the target ring. CONTROLS: Click a ball to hop, then click a destination to move it. RULE: A square is valid only if its four corners land on black terrain. TRAP: Moving balls simultaneously breaks the sequence; you must complete one ball's path before starting the next.

GOAL: Rotate and position the yellow piece to bridge the green and purple shapes, connecting their free tips. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space rotates it; Clicks select which piece to control. RULE: Only the active piece displays red tips on free ends; inactive pieces blend tips with their own color. TRAP: Assuming all free tips appear red leads to misidentifying inactive pieces; inactive tips match the piece’s body color.

GOAL: Place shapes and adjust reflection axes to align solid copies with sparse yellow targets, accepting inevitable block spillage. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected pieces or shift mirror axes; clicks select pieces or confirm placement. RULE: Reflections are rigid mirrors across the bar’s center line, creating fixed charcoal duplicates that dictate valid positioning. TRAP: Assuming solid shapes fit perfectly into dotted patterns; they often overflow boundaries, so focus on axis alignment rather than gapless coverage.

ESTABLISHED: You occupy odd coordinates. Orange patrols column 13, sliding vertically. The goal is at (7,7). FAILED: Assuming simultaneous moves are safe without checking path intersections; direct movement into orange's current cell causes death. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the orange's current position or waiting for it to stop moving. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move two spaces. Blocked moves consume a turn. Crossing the orange's swept path kills you.

GOAL: Find and absorb hidden plugs to unlock matching sockets on the side panel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character to overlap and absorb items; mouse clicks activate unlocked sockets. RULE: Plugs are only visible or reachable once you enter their specific color-coded box area. TRAP: Do not assume obstacles are permanent; activating a matching socket transforms checker patterns into solid paths.

GOAL: Guide four blocks into matching hollow rings. CONTROLS: Arrows drive the selected block; clicks select a block. RULE: A block stays driven until you select another. TRAP: Clicking a block again resets its drive, wasting turns.

ESTABLISHED: Successful shadow moves set the plug's direction; blocked clicks do not change it. FAILED: Toggling specific hexes or clicking inactive boxes failed to redirect the plug or trigger the goal. GOAL IS NOT: Activating the plug with the current leftward setting; the level resets if actions run out. CONTROLS: Clicking boxes moves shadows or sets direction; clicking hexes toggles states; the ball triggers movement.

GOAL: Route the green marker past a wall by clearing the path first. CONTROLS: Click side panels to extend or shrink shape lengths; click center to move. RULE: Shapes cannot pass through walls, so you must shrink the green body to fit above the obstacle before moving it right. TRAP: Assuming the green’s current length could squeeze past the wall, causing blocked moves until it was manually shortened.

GOAL: Guide two squares to meet by opening colored gates. CONTROLS: Arrows move both squares simultaneously in the same direction. RULE: Standing on a token opens all gates of that matching color. TRAP: Assuming leaving a token keeps gates open; they snap shut immediately, trapping you.

GOAL: Shrink the blob, navigate past the socket, and enter the knob. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicks reshape the body. RULE: Clicking specific points shrinks the tip to its top-left quadrant. TRAP: Moving before shrinking wastes actions and blocks the path through the door.

ESTABLISHED: The camera scrolls up when the player rises. FAILED: Relying on purple block positions for alignment. GOAL IS NOT: A simple vertical climb. CONTROLS: LEFT and RIGHT move the player; the camera follows upward movements.

GOAL: Align four geometric pieces to form a connected structure with zero overlap. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces, clicks select targets, and Space rotates the active piece. RULE: Pieces must touch exactly at their designated junction points without intersecting. TRAP: Assuming intermediate moves could create temporary overlaps; paths must remain valid at every step to avoid rejection.

ESTABLISHED: The socket moves one cell per press, strictly following the wire path; it cannot clip through walls or move off the wire. FAILED: Pressing arrows that do not align with the wire's direction resulted in no movement. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing any cross in the socket; the specific configuration required for panel B remains elusive. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the socket one step along the connected wire; invalid directions do nothing.

ESTABLISHED: Two distinct dot pairs exist, one near the left edge and one on the right. A purple piece is already assembled. FAILED: Attempting to merge distant pairs directly fails; dots must be moved close enough before clicking between them. GOAL IS NOT: A single large merge or simply clearing the screen of dots without specific pairings. CONTROLS: Clicking near a dot moves it toward the cursor. Clicking exactly between two close dots merges them.

GOAL: Align the glyph symbol to unlock the door and reach the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; the plus symbol rotates the nearby glyph. RULE: The door only opens when the glyph matches the required pattern. TRAP: Assuming the door stays open after one rotation; it closes if the glyph is misaligned again.

GOAL: Fit every block into the matching ring. CONTROLS: Arrows slide pieces or push neighbors along straight paths. RULE: Pushing a piece into a ring locks it, so solve tight spots first. TRAP: Assuming blocks stop immediately; they slide until hitting a wall or another piece, so check clear paths before pushing.

GOAL: Decode the tile glyphs to match the target pattern and clear the board. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selector; pressing them cycles the highlighted tile’s symbol through a fixed sequence. RULE: Each color group shares one hidden symbol dictionary, so identical shapes must always mean the same letter. TRAP: Assuming two-symbol bars change glyphs independently wastes moves; they actually rotate as a single locked pair.

GOAL: Fill the lower half purple and top half white using overlapping press zones. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the press cursor; Space applied the current ink color; Clicks changed the ink color. RULE: Presses only affected cells within their specific directional wedge, leaving outside areas untouched. TRAP: Assuming you needed to restore specific white cells; actually, the final top press overwrote them, so only the bottom coverage mattered.

ESTABLISHED: The guard settles at the top-left slot. You can stand directly above the frame without overlapping the guard. Boxes naturally slide into empty slots when you block their path. FAILED: Mirroring previous positions or moving too far right fails to divert boxes correctly. GOAL IS NOT: A static puzzle; it requires dynamic positioning to guide moving objects. CONTROLS: Move to block paths. Wait to let physics settle boxes. Intervene only if a box gets stuck outside the frame.

ESTABLISHED: A purple handle sits in panel four, adjacent to a left-wall marker. Water levels differ between the marker and the handle box. FAILED: Aligning the handle box strictly one row above or below the marker failed to solve the puzzle. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing the box at the marker's exact row or assuming the water covers the marker. CONTROLS: Moving the handle shifts the box vertically. Adjusting the water level changes the reference point for the box position.

GOAL: Navigate a narrow path by sliding over hazards to reach the exit before your energy runs out. CONTROLS: Arrows move and slide your character; clicks activate specific tiles to clear the way. RULE: Sliding continues until you hit a wall, so plan your stopping point before moving. TRAP: Believing you can stop mid-slide wastes actions; you must position yourself correctly before launching.

GOAL: Deliver the box by collecting two plus signs and a dial while managing limited fuel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; visiting refill stations restores fuel capacity. RULE: Fuel drains with every step, forcing you to visit refill points to reach distant targets. TRAP: Assuming you can visit refill stations out of order or skip required item collections before reaching the exit.

GOAL: Guide the tip to the knob before actions run out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the tip; direction does not gate movement. RULE: The tip moves immediately in the pressed direction, ignoring its facing. TRAP: Believing you must turn before moving wastes actions; just press toward the target.

GOAL: Color the 10x10 grid into white, purple, and orange zones by moving a die to specific corners and pressing keys. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the die; clicks select a color; space applies the selected color to the die's current region. RULE: Each die position paints a fixed geometric area; overlapping presses overwrite previous colors, so final order determines the result. TRAP: Assuming moves are reversible without checking the die's exact bounding box led to wasted actions when a move was a no-op.

GOAL: Guide the glowing socket along the wire to the target ring. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the socket; clicking the socket selects it for the final jump. RULE: The socket follows the wire’s path exactly; you cannot cut corners or leave the track. TRAP: Thinking there was a move limit caused unnecessary panic; the energy bar capped harmlessly without failing the level.

GOAL: Paint the canvas by stamping ink from a rolling die onto matching zones. CONTROLS: Arrows roll the die; clicks select ink colors; Space stamps the current face. RULE: Stamp only when the die’s visible face matches the target zone’s color. TRAP: Assuming the small die stays fixed; it actually moves with the main die, requiring precise positioning.

GOAL: Arrange blocks to form a specific chain sequence on the board. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected block one step in that direction. RULE: Blocks link only when adjacent in the correct order, connecting to the head. TRAP: Assuming the arm’s length matters; it does not, only relative block positions count.

GOAL: Cover three dial spots, grab the ring for energy, and push the box home. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; stepping on objects activates them. RULE: Stepping on a ring instantly refills the energy bar, granting vital slack for the final push. TRAP: Going straight to the box leaves zero margin; skipping the ring guarantees failure.

GOAL: Apply orange, purple, and blue dyes in that strict order to specific zones. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the large die; clicking a color swatch selects it; Space presses it down. RULE: Each press overwrites previous colors in its area, so the final blue press must happen last. TRAP: Assuming the small die is stuck to the large one; it slides independently when clicked.

GOAL: Color the board by painting quadrants in a specific sequence to achieve the final pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor, clicks select ink or tools, and space presses the current location. RULE: Overlapping colors overwrite previous ones, so the final visible color depends on the last paint applied to that area. TRAP: Assuming paint order is irrelevant; painting the wrong quadrant last ruins the result because later strokes erase earlier ones.
